company.name: Allbirds
company.oneLiner: Allbirds sells shoes, socks, and apparel made from wool, tree fiber, and sugarcane, mainly direct to consumers online.
company.customers: Men and women buying everyday sneakers, slip-ons, flats, and sandals online, plus shoppers who buy through other retailers.

blueprint.headline: Allbirds can give its merchandising, planning and support teams back hours each week and protect margin by having agents draft sale plans, size-level reorder lists, and exchange offers that a person only approves.

agents.name: Size-Level Reorder List
agents.role: Builds a purchase order draft for each style and size so the inventory planner does not assemble it by hand.

value.today: The planner exports sales and stock by style and size into a spreadsheet, compares them with supplier lead times, and builds the purchase order line by line.
value.sizing: Number of styles x sizes per style x share of sizes that end up overstocked or sold out per season x average margin or markdown loss per pair

agents.impact: Stops the overbuying of slow sizes and the sell-outs of fast ones across Wool Runner, Tree Runner NZ and the rest of the range, so less cash sits in unsold pairs and fewer sales are lost.
agents.trigger: Every Monday at 07:00 local, and on demand before a sale event.
does: Reads sales and on-hand stock for each style and size
Projects cover against supplier lead time and planned sale events
Drafts a reorder list with quantities by size for each style
Flags sizes to stop reordering as ready-to-mark-down candidates

humanGate.detail: The planner approves every purchase order before it goes to a supplier; the agent only saves drafts.

agents.evidence: The site sells many styles (Wool Runner, Tree Breezer, Cruiser, Terralux Collection, Socks) with many size variants and SKUs per style.

agents.name: Sale Event Markdown Plan
agents.role: Drafts which styles and sizes to discount, by how much, and when, for Black Friday, holiday and other sales.

value.today: The merchandiser pulls stock and sell-through into a spreadsheet, picks discount levels from past sales and gut feel, and then lists each product for the site team.
value.sizing: Number of sale events per year x units of aged stock per event x average price recovered per unit versus a blanket discount

agents.impact: Clears aging stock at the shallowest discount that still moves it and keeps full price on fast sellers, so each sale earns more per pair.
agents.trigger: Four weeks before each planned sale event, and on demand.
does: Reads stock cover and sell-through by style and size
Sets a proposed discount tier for each style, keeping fast sellers at full price
Drafts the sale price list and a short promo calendar by category
Estimates units and revenue per tier from past sale periods

humanGate.detail: The merchandising manager approves every price change and discount tier before anything is published to the store.

agents.evidence: The profile notes frequent seasonal sales including Black Friday and holiday sales, with men's and women's ranges across many categories.

agents.name: Return Exchange Offer Draft
agents.role: Reads each return request and drafts a reply that offers the right size exchange within the policy.

value.today: A support agent reads each return email, looks up the order, checks the 15-day window and tags, and types out the return or exchange steps.
value.sizing: Return and exchange emails per week x minutes to look up the order and write the reply / 60

agents.impact: Cuts the hours the support team spends typing out return steps, and turns some refunds into size exchanges that keep the sale.
agents.trigger: When a new email about a return or exchange arrives in the support inbox.
does: Reads the email and finds the matching order
Checks the 15-day window, unworn condition, country of purchase, and return coverage
Drafts a reply with the correct steps, and a size exchange offer where it fits
Queues the draft with the order details beside it

humanGate.detail: Every reply to a customer is reviewed by a support agent, and any refund or exception outside the 15-day policy waits for the support lead.

agents.evidence: The site states a 15-day return policy for unworn items with tags, customer-paid return shipping unless coverage is bought, in-country returns only, and support by email.

firstBuild.why: Support hours are the easiest payoff to see, the policy is written down and fixed, and the agent only drafts replies, so risk and integration work are low.
scope: Read incoming return and exchange emails from the support inbox
Match each email to an order and check the 15-day, tags and country rules
Draft replies from approved wording with the exchange size offer
Queue drafts for agent review with order facts alongside
Track how many drafts are sent unedited

blueprint.nonObvious: With a 15-day window, paid return shipping and refunds only to the original payment, every wrong-size return costs Allbirds twice: the refund and the shipping and handling of a pair that may come back unsellable, so turning returns into size exchanges is worth more than answering faster.
caveats: Sales volume, margin, and team size were not visible; sizing formulas use the owner's own records.
Assumed an ecommerce platform, inventory system and email help desk exist, but none was named.
Assumed purchasing runs on supplier lead times and spreadsheets, which the profile does not show.
Loyalty program details were not visible and were not used.
